title: Normalization and strict diagrams for open tensor coefficients
statement: For the open total-tensor coefficient data [def-sf-open-total-tensor-coefficient-data], define normalization to mean that $\gamma$ and its inverse send $[x]_f\otimes y$ to $[x\otimes j^*y]_f$ and back, $r$ and its inverse send $[x]_f\otimes a$ to $[x\otimes a|]_f$ and back, and the restriction/scalar comparison keeps scalar tensor sections. Define the left composite $\gamma^A(r\otimes1)b^X$ and the right composite $j_{A!}(b^V)r(\gamma^R\otimes1)$ from $X_A$ to $Y_A$. A strict coefficient family is a functor on unital $R$-algebra sheaves with values, after actual scalar restriction [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars], in $R$-complexes; its identity and composition equations are literal. Define strictness of coefficient-linear isomorphisms by the corresponding naturality squares and package these as a natural isomorphism. For strict inverse towers [def-weil-inverse-system], transpose towers of complexes to complexes of towers and use the standard derived localization in that abelian functor category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Define the source and target maps induced by two chain maps using the existing functors and total tensor.
